requirements.evidence: CreateQueue trims the name, slugifies an explicit or default slug, checks entity-scoped uniqueness and maps unique QueryException to ValidationException (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:62-93). UpdateQueue uses nullable named params and Rule::unique()->ignore($queue->id) (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:216-253). SetQueueAccess upserts or deletes, validates 'permissions.*' => required|string|in, checks for a cross-entity mismatch and does not log a revoke when $deleted is 0 (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:142-192). The QueuePolicy call ability denies non-array permissions (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:533-536). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:31). Ticket::call orders lock queue -> inactive -> authorize -> waiting check (app/Models/Ticket.php:432-459). Migration, enum, model and factory match the contract. Small gaps: the factory silently moves a membership to another entity, the grant log fires even when nothing changed, and duplicate permission entries are stored as given.

conventions.evidence: Positives: domain writes are in app/Actions, authorization goes through the auto-discovered QueuePolicy via Gate::forUser, #[Fillable] is set on QueueAccess (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:364), and docs and CHANGELOG are updated. Clear deviations: the diff contains no test at all, which breaks the 'No production code without a test' TDD rule. The migration name 2026_09_07_000000_create_queue_access_table.php has a zeroed time part, which suggests it was written by hand instead of with make:migration.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes first: CreateQueue.php:60, UpdateQueue.php:223 and SetQueueAccess.php:140. Both call paths enforce the policy (CallNextTicket.php:31, Ticket.php:444). Permission input is validated against the enum (SetQueueAccess.php:150-163) and cross-entity grants are rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:142). Mass assignment is restricted with #[Fillable]. Minor: isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (FK or NOT NULL as well) as a slug duplicate, but this only affects the error message. No exploitable flaw found.

tests.evidence: The diff adds no file under tests/. No coverage for queue creation or update, slug uniqueness, races, SetQueueAccess validation, audit logging, policy abilities, or the new authorization in CallNextTicket and Ticket::call. Existing tests that relied on 'any entity member can call' (the old Ticket.php membership check) are also not updated in the diff.

simplicity.evidence: The isUniqueViolation helper is copied verbatim in CreateQueue.php:96-106 and UpdateQueue.php:278-288. QueueAccessFactory::configure (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:586-605) adds an afterMaking hook that rewrites and saves the membership's entity_id, which is extra machinery the definition-level closure already covers. Two relations nothing uses are added: Queue::accesses and EntityMembership::queueAccesses. The rest is direct and lean.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and the methods are small. The policy has a docblock on each ability and an isManagerOf helper (QueuePolicy.php:539). The Ticket::call docblock is updated (Ticket.php:424-425). In UpdateQueue the separate $attributes and $rules building blocks (UpdateQueue.php:225-254) are a little verbose but easy to follow. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Everything serves the task, and there is no delete action. Minor extras: the inverse relations Queue::accesses (app/Models/Queue.php:343) and EntityMembership::queueAccesses (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:323), which nothing uses.

issues.explanation: The change adds actions, a policy, a model, a migration and new authorization on two call paths without a single Pest test, which violates the project's mandatory TDD rule.
Ticket::call now denies employees without a grant, where before any entity member could call, but the diff updates no existing tests that relied on the old behaviour, so the suite may break.
The isUniqueViolation helper is duplicated verbatim in two actions.

The afterMaking hook silently moves an already-persisted membership to the queue's entity, and it writes to the DB even on make(). This can hide test setup mistakes and could collide with the single-owner index.
The zeroed timestamp suggests the migration was written by hand rather than generated with make:migration, as the conventions require.
SQLSTATE 23000 covers every integrity violation (FK, NOT NULL), so non-unique DB errors would be misreported as a slug duplicate.
The inverse relations accesses() and queueAccesses() are not required by the task and are not used.
Duplicate entries such as ['call','call'] are stored as given instead of being de-duplicated.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess, a QueuePolicy, the queue_access table, model and factory, and it enforces the call ability in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with docs and CHANGELOG updated. The production code is correct and follows the Actions-plus-policy pattern well. However, it ships no tests at all, against the project's mandatory TDD convention, and it duplicates the unique-violation helper, so it needs changes before merging.
